transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: James (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Aisha (Stonebridge SecOps), Tom (CTO), Ellen (Compliance), Raj (Platform)
Shared artifacts: link: https://drive.redwood/reports/stonebridge-poc-security-pack.pdf ; sheet: https://sheets.redwood/stonebridge-pilot-benchmarks

Summary:
Quick weekly sync focused on security/compliance checkpoints for the POC: SSO/SAML, audit logs, data retention/residency, and SOC 2 paperwork. Agreed next steps include Redwood sharing SOC 2 attestation and a short audit-log demo using anonymized sample traffic. Customer to provide retention policy and list of regions with regulatory requirements.

Topics:
- SSO integration status (IdP metadata, SAML attributes)
- Audit logging granularity and retention (who can see what, export options)
- Data retention / deletion workflows and residency controls
- SOC 2 documentation and pen test notes
- Performance impact of logging for high-throughput test cases

Action items (recorded above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] James Ortega: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time today. quick readout: we'll go through SSO, audit logs, retention, and then any questions. sound good?
[00:14] Aisha Malik: yep that works for us. we've got a few security folks on the line but i'll hand it to tom for any infra specifics.
[00:23] Tom Becker: hey all, thanks. main thing for us this week is understanding what audit payload looks like at token level, and how long we can keep it in case of investigations - regulatory will want 7 years for certain records.
[00:36] Priya Nair: okay, great. quick status: we pulled the SAML metadata you sent, and the IdP config seems straightforward. a couple of mapping questions - the NameID format you currently send is email, is there a requirement to send groups as a separate attribute?
[00:50] Raj Patel: we do rely on groups for role mapping, yes. our current IdP pins group membership and we need those mapped to RBAC roles in Redwood's console.
[01:02] Priya Nair: understood. we can map groups to roles; we have both SAML attrmap and SCIM available. SCIM would give you direct group sync but that requires extra onboarding.
[01:15] Ellen Park: is SCIM mandatory for audit purposes? we'd prefer to avoid extra wide access but we need reliable group sync.
[01:24] Liam Chen: scoping note: scim is optional; many customers use SAML attr mappings for pilots. SCIM just reduces drift for long-term deployments.
[01:36] Aisha Malik: also need to confirm session timeout policies - we can't have 24-hour sessions for privileged accounts.
[01:44] James Ortega: yeah, we have configurable session TTLs per role; default is 8 hours but we can set lower for admin roles. we'll include that in the config doc.
[01:56] Tom Becker: perfect. next, audit logs - what do those look like for token-level events? request, response, model, tokens consumed?
[02:07] Priya Nair: good question. Redwood emits structured audit events: request meta (caller id, route, model, prompts hashes), response meta (tokens consumed, truncated flag), and system events (deployment changes, role grants). we can stream logs to your SIEM via HTTPS or push to S3.
[02:30] Raj Patel: how verbose is the prompt in those logs? we can't ship full prompt text offsite for PII reasons.
[02:38] Priya Nair: prompts are configurable. by default we redact user-submitted PII and store a hashed prompt fingerprint. but during the pilot, if you want to capture full prompts for debugging we can do it in a private VPC mode or with customer-managed KMS to encrypt logs.
[02:56] Aisha Malik: hmm ok that matters. legal will want proof we didn't exfiltrate any sensitive prompts. can Redwood provide a certified flow for on-prem or VPC-hosted logging?
[03:08] James Ortega: yes, for Private deployments we support customer VPC connectors and you can also use our Private package which keeps logs in your S3 and under your KMS. for hosted pilots we do offer an option to ship logs to your S3 with an encryption-at-rest key that you manage.
[03:24] Ellen Park: do you have SOC 2 type II? we need the report and an executive summary.
[03:30] James Ortega: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II; i'll share the summary and link to the attestation after the call. expect that in your inbox within 48 hours.
[03:41] Tom Becker: great. any pen test reports?
[03:45] Priya Nair: we have pen test highlights and remediation notes; we don't share full third-party pentest reports unless there's an NDA but we can provide a summary doc.
[03:54] Aisha Malik: ok please include the remediation timeline for the last two issues.
[03:58] James Ortega: noted.
[04:02] Raj Patel: about retention - we need configurable retention per artifact type. e.g., audit logs for admin events 7 years, request logs 90 days, embeddings maybe 1 year. can Redwood set per-stream retention?
[04:17] Priya Nair: yes, retention is per-log stream and per-bucket. on hosted mode we offer retention tiers and deletion workflows. in Private mode you control retention in your S3 lifecycle rules.
[04:30] Ellen Park: what's the deletion workflow? can we trigger ad-hoc deletes for specific sessions?
[04:36] Priya Nair: we support on-demand deletions by request id or session id and have a delete API that triggers deletion across caches and logs. note there's also KV cache TTL for model context which is separate; that can be expired immediately or left to its TTL depending on your needs.
[04:52] Tom Becker: any regulatory holds? if we need to freeze data for an investigation, is there a legal hold process?
[04:59] Liam Chen: there's a legal-hold flow where we export data and prevent lifecycle deletes; for hosted customers we can apply holds at object-level in the archive bucket. documenting the process is part of our compliance pack.
[05:12] Aisha Malik: performance question: logging everything will increase latency and cost. have you measured the token-level logging overhead?
[05:21] Priya Nair: yes, we did perf runs. basic structured audit logging adds ~10-20ms p50 overhead for small requests. if you stream full prompts and heavy payloads overhead could go to 40-60ms. we can also batch and async ship logs to minimize tail latency.
[05:40] Tom Becker: that's acceptable if documented. can we get the perf spreadsheet?
[05:44] James Ortega: shared link in chat - we'll push the perf sheet.
[05:48] (brief crosstalk)
[06:05] Raj Patel: about encryption keys - if you manage the KMS, do you rotate keys on our schedule?
[06:11] Priya Nair: for customer-managed KMS we honor your rotation schedule; Redwood's runtime can be configured to use your KMS for log encryption. for on-prem installations, keys never leave your HSM.
[06:23] Ellen Park: are there role-based audit views? e.g., SecOps sees more metadata than product dev?
[06:30] Liam Chen: yes RBAC is integrated into the console and audit access is layered. we can create restricted views for developers so they only see anonymous telemetry while SecOps sees full audit metadata.
[06:44] Aisha Malik: excellent. one more point: can you provide an example of the audit schema? we need field names to map to our SIEM parsers.
[06:53] Priya Nair: absolutely, we'll attach the audit schema JSON as a separate artifact. it includes fields: event_type, timestamp, actor_id, route, model_id, token_count, prompt_hash, response_status, context_tags. note some field names in our docs might have hyphens or camelCase; our schema doc will include both variants we've seen in different exports, apologies in advance for any inconsistency.
[07:18] Tom Becker: that's fine. next, when you say prompt_hash, what's the hash algorithm?
[07:23] Priya Nair: we use SHA256 by default; we also support a truncated SHA1 fingerprint for legacy parsers.
[07:30] Raj Patel: for our audit we need immutable logs - are logs tamper-evident?
[07:35] Priya Nair: yes we support append-only logs with signed manifests; when pushed to your S3 we can also enable object-lock to prevent modification.
[07:45] Aisha Malik: and access logs for admin console - who changed RBAC, who created new keys?
[07:52] Liam Chen: all admin actions are recorded. we can correlate console events to the audit stream for a full chain of custody.
[07:59] Ellen Park: what about data residency - if a prompt touches EU PII we need it to stay in eu-west-1. can Redwood route regionally?
[08:09] Priya Nair: yes, routing policies exist. you can pin workloads to a region and we have guardrails that keep data in that region if you're on Dedicated or Private. Hosted mode has region controls for data locality but for strict residency we recommend Redwood Private with a dedicated region deployment.
[08:28] Tom Becker: do we need a full private deployment for the pilot to satisfy our compliance team?
[08:33] Aisha Malik: for now pilot-level, maybe we can do a hosted pilot but ensure logs are pushed to our EU S3 and keys are customer-managed; full Private could be next phase.
[08:45] James Ortega: that's a common pattern: hosted pilot with customer-managed S3 + KMS, then private for production.
[08:52] Raj Patel: on the topic of deletion: if we ask to delete specific user sessions, how long until downstream caches expire?
[08:59] Priya Nair: deletion triggers cache purge requests; KV cache purge is near-real-time but depends on active model context. worst-case TTL is a minute or two for active contexts; we'll document the expected window.
[09:14] Tom Becker: good. any blockers on the SSO side?
[09:17] Raj Patel: we sent our metadata but missing one attribute mapping: we need "stonebridge:department" to map to team tags.
[09:24] Priya Nair: we'll add that attr mapping. i'll send a sample SAML mapping snippet after the call.
[09:31] Aisha Malik: about timeline - legal wants SOC2 docs before pilot expansion next month.
[09:36] James Ortega: we'll prioritize SOC2 summary and put attestation link in your shared folder.
[09:40] Ellen Park: also can we get a short recording of an audit-log demo that shows search and export flows?
[09:47] Priya Nair: yes, we'll record a 10-15 minute demo and share a private link.
[09:52] Tom Becker: one last concern—competitor comparison: BigCloudAI was offering them pipeline-level logging but they push everything into their own SIEM; we prefer Redwood's customer S3 model.
[10:05] James Ortega: understood, we'll make the architecture comparison explicit in the doc we send.
[10:12] (brief hold as participants check links)
[10:38] Liam Chen: recap of next steps: SOC 2 docs, audit-log demo recording, SAML attr map snippet, retention policy from Stonebridge.
[10:49] Aisha Malik: yep thanks, that works.
[10:53] James Ortega: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the demo for next week.
[11:00] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker label mismatches and cut words; some product names transcribed inconsistently (e.g., "KV cache" as "K-V cash" in one spot).
